extractedText: Breadcrumb Research The Chinese Communist Party’s Layered Artificial Intelligence Strategy The Chinese Communist Party’s Layered Artificial Intelligence Strategy July 21, 2025 Image Download article Executive Summary Artificial intelligence is at the core of the Chinese Communist Party’s (CPC) vision for national security and technological self-reliance. Over the course of decades, Chinese leaders have developed layers of national policy that align government agencies, private companies, the military, and academia on the development and implementation of this emerging technology. China’s AI ecosystem is rapidly developing technological breakthroughs that expand its global influence—and the political control of the CPC. Today, China’s centrally planned AI strategy has made it a peer competitor with the US, whose less regulated AI ecosystem is mostly led by private tech companies. China’s rapid rise in this field begs important questions. How did the CPC’s ambitious AI strategy take shape? What strengths does China’s top-down approach to AI domination have, and what are its vulnerabilities? What institutional and economic frictions could impede China from becoming the world leader in AI innovation? This paper tackles these questions and more by examining the full scope of CPC policies guiding AI development. By mapping national strategies, historical context, and institutional actors, our researchers provides a foundation for analysts and policymakers to understand how AI fits into China’s broader goals of state control, global competitiveness, and innovative government. Key Takeaways: The CPC built and layered its AI strategy atop decades of ideological and institutional planning. From Deng Xiaoping’s reform era to Xi Jinping’s digital governance, China developed AI not as a standalone policy initiative, but rather folded it into evolving doctrines of modernization, centralization, and techno-political control. The CPC sees AI as a strategic asset to reinforce, not disrupt, party dominance. In addition to being a transformative industrial tool, AI is embedded in authoritarian governance as an ideological instrument used for surveillance, censorship, and “social governance” purposes that align with CPC interests. China has created a vertically integrated pipeline that draws behavioral, transactional, and biometric data from smart cities, social platforms, healthcare systems and finance, then curates this data for AI modeling and governance. However, CPC pressure has historically led to self-censorship and misreporting, so this data could be biased and unreliable. In addition to political bias in AI inputs, vulnerabilities in the Chinese AI strategy include bureaucratic tensions like institutional rivalries and regulatory contradictions. Local governments also face policy ambiguities and have uneven resources across provinces, hindering national coordination.
